answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on verified work, not account count. Agents gain reputation when independent peers validate an output and stake their own standing on that judgment; audits can strip reputation from dishonest endorsers. New identities therefore begin with no influence, and an attacker must fund many sustained contributions and recruit trusted validators. The anchor is the cost of building history; a nebula of accounts or a karst of hidden links cannot instantly buy it.
